title: Code and data for: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe

creators.name: Zhang, Alan
creators.affiliation: McMaster University; Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics

description:
Code, archived production results and figure scripts that reproduce the numbers and figures of two papers on a small flat universe (cubic three-torus) that begins at a Casimir turning point: Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins (a Letter, arXiv:2610.28704) and A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe (arXiv:2610.24905).

Four chains of result directories: casimir/ (Standard-Model Casimir weight, gauge/Higgs zero-mode energy, shape Hessian), higgs/ (finite-volume Higgs zero-mode criterion: SM couplings at the turning-point scale, one-loop finite-volume matching, 2D zero-mode model with cross terms, hazard integral, critical top-quark masses and error budget, real-time xi_H condition, robustness, universality, two-branch analysis), shape/ (emptiness gate, real-moment theorem, shape fossil, nonlinear survival, Moyal and Wheeler-DeWitt checks, primordial spectra) and cmb/ (T+E covariance of a three-torus, Fisher information and exact KL divergences, fossil ensemble, joint inflaton-shape state). Every result directory has a quick and a full mode and compares fresh output with the archived production values (expected/) under stated tolerances; python run_all.py --quick reproduces the quick checks and all figures.

validation/ archives the independent reimplementations of the results (blind and compute-first checks, with their specifications, code and outputs) and compares them with the main calculation; cmb/02_ensemble/data/ ships the l <= 80 CAMB transfer table.

Code: MIT. Data and text: CC BY 4.0. SMDR 1.3 (tarball shipped unmodified) and the four files derived from it (higgs/01_sm_mapping/c148_fit.c, higgs/zmlib/_smdr_betas.py, validation/sm_mapping/code/drivers/c148_fit_copy.c and smdr_driver.c): GPL-2.0-or-later.

The companion technical report (Casimir Cosmology: Derivations and Numerical Validation) is deposited as a separate Zenodo record (publication/report, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23434140), which the papers cite; a copy is included here in docs/technical_report/.
references: A. Zhang, Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins, a Letter, arXiv:2610.28704 (2026)
A. Zhang, A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe, arXiv:2610.24905 (2026)
S.P. Martin and D.G. Robertson, SMDR (Standard Model in Dimensional Regularization) version 1.3, https://www.niu.edu/spmartin/SMDR/, arXiv:1907.02500
